# Suddhaṭṭhaka Sutta (Snp 4.4 (PTS Snp 154))
**ID:** Snp 4.4 (PTS Snp 154)
**Section:** Suttanipāta (snp)
**Collection:** Suttas-Early-2
**Title (Pali):** Suddhaṭṭhaka Sutta
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/snp4.4
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0505m.mul3.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Suddhaṭṭhaka Sutta* ("Eight on the Pure") is the fourth discourse of the *Aṭṭhakavagga* in the *Suttanipāta* (Snp 4.4, PTS Snp 154, verses 788–795) [Anderson & Smith 1913; Max Müller 1881; Norman 1997-2001; SuttaCentral]. It is one of only four poems in the collection that strictly fulfill the designation of an *aṭṭhaka* by comprising exactly eight verses [Hazra 1994]. The sutta addresses the trap of abandoning one attachment only to grasp after something more subtle, warning against the dogmatic claim that purity comes from what is seen or speculative views [Hazra 1994; Ñāṇananda; SuttaCentral]. It emphasizes that theoretical philosophical systems cannot purify a person, noting that those clinging to dogmas drift from teacher to teacher; in contrast, the detached sage (*muni* or *brāhmaṇa*) does not grasp views, remains free from passion, and has overcome dispute [Hazra 1994; Max Müller 1881; Ruegg & Schmithausen 1990]. Verse 792 specifically criticizes those attached to apperception (*saññāsatta*), contrasting them with one who understands the Dhamma and possesses wisdom [Ruegg & Schmithausen 1990].
A full canonical commentary on the text is preserved in the *Mahāniddesa* (Mnd 4, *Suddhaṭṭhakasuttaniddesa*) [Hazra 1994; SuttaCentral; Sujin Boriharnwanaket]. SuttaCentral identifies an early Chinese parallel in the *Yizu jing* (T 198) [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus finds 64 text-reuse matches across four Pali texts, the vast majority shared with its canonical commentary in Mnd 4 (44 matches, up to 3,615 characters), alongside citations and commentary in the *Suttanipāta-aṭṭhakathā*, the *Mahāniddesa-aṭṭhakathā*, and the *Mahābyūhasuttaniddesa* (Mnd 13) [DharmaNexus]. No cross-language matches met the reporting threshold in DharmaNexus [DharmaNexus].
